pages.title: Intelligent Identification Method of Low Voltage AC Series Arc Fault Based on Using Residual Model and Rime Optimization Algorithm
pages.authors: Xiao He, Takahiro Kawaguchi and Seiji Hashimoto *
pages.abstract: Aiming at the problem of accurate AC series arc fault detection, this paper proposes a low voltage AC series arc fault intelligent detection model based on deep learning. According to the GB/T 31143-2014 standard, an experimental platform was established. This system comprises a lower computer and an upper computer. Based on a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Residual model (Res) and RIME optimization algorithm are introduced to optimize the CNN. Experimental results indicate that the RIME optimization algorithm delivers the best performance when optimizing a one-dimensional CNN with introduced Res, achieving 99.42% accuracy.
pages.keywords: series arc fault; Convolutional Neural Network (CNN); Residual model (Res); RIME

paragraphs.text: Introduction

sentences.text: Introduction

paragraphs.text: Due to the impact of different circuit and load types, the current magnitude associated with arc faults varies. Series arc faults, in particular, generate lower currents compared to parallel and ground arc faults, making them more difficult for circuit breakers to detect. This challenge in detection can prevent timely circuit disconnection, increasing the risk of electrical fires. Therefore, effective intelligent detection of AC series arc faults under various operating conditions is critical for reducing the likelihood of electrical fires. Currently, arc fault detection methods are categorized into three main types.

paragraphs.subchapter_title: Fault Arc Detection Method Based on Mathematical Modeling
paragraphs.text: Traditional arc models are used to describe the electrical characteristics, behavior, and impact of arcs for fault detection and protection in power systems. Common models include the empirical model, Elmore model, Sato model, and Mayr model. Each model has its own strengths and limitations, and the choice of model depends on the specific application requirements, operating conditions, and desired accuracy. D. Lee and J. Kim conducted empirical modeling of arc faults based on experimental data [1]. T. Carter and J. Wang analyzed high-current arc faults on power systems based on the Elmore model [2].

Lee introduced acoustic emission technology in arc fault detection [12].

paragraphs.subchapter_title: Fault Arc Detection Method Based on Electrical Signals
paragraphs.text: With the increasing variety of household appliances, arcs can occur during their operation, and the distribution of these appliances is random. This randomness makes it challenging to pinpoint the exact location of an arc fault. When an arc fault occurs, the current and voltage signals in the circuit become distorted and are not necessarily indicative of the arc's location. Therefore, detecting arc faults by measuring the circuit's current and voltage signals has become a widely used method. Current research focuses on signal selection, effective feature extraction, and intelligent recognition using machine learning models.

paragraphs.text: Arc Fault Detection Model

sentences.text: Arc Fault Detection Model

paragraphs.text: There are many types of arc fault detection models. This paper proposes a low-voltage AC series arc detection model based on a one-dimensional convolutional neural network incorporating residual modules and the frost optimization algorithm. This detection model uses extracted time-domain, frequency-domain, and wavelet packet energy features as inputs. It was trained, validated, and tested on an established experimental data set. Experimental results show that this arc fault detection model has high detection accuracy.

pages.title: Cognitive Load Reduction in Academic Reading
pages.authors: Dr. Elena Rostova, Prof. Marcus Chen
pages.abstract: The split-attention effect has been widely recognized as a primary cognitive bottleneck when graduate students engage with dense mathematical literature. In this paper, an in-situ reading environment is introduced to eliminate context-switching penalties. Empirical evaluations demonstrate a 42% acceleration in comprehension speed.

paragraphs.text: Introduction

sentences.text: Introduction

paragraphs.text: Traditional digital reading environments were developed under the document-centric paradigm of physical paper reproduction. Consequently, supplementary derivations are relegated to footnotes, sidebars, or external browser tabs. When complex scientific papers are investigated, working memory is rapidly saturated by the necessity of holding antecedent propositions in mind. As demonstrated by Chen et al. (2024), cognitive friction is significantly heightened whenever multi-column layouts force erratic saccadic movements. To mitigate this issue, structured sentence decomposition is urgently required.

paragraphs.text: To attenuate these cognitive obstacles, our system incorporates deep linguistic parsing. Passive voice constructions are systematically identified by dependency grammar analyzers. Subsequently, conceptual intuition lenses are generated on demand using large language model synthesis. Empirical benchmarks indicate that extraneous cognitive load is attenuated by 38% across diverse reader cohorts. Furthermore, orthogonal semantic pathways facilitate deeper structural synthesis.
